subject: RQTL2 questions; LOD plot marker ticks, lod scores manipulation and citation preferences...

messages.author: dd9e1ba32313d2a3
messages.subject: RQTL2 questions; LOD plot marker ticks, lod scores manipulation and citation preferences...
parts:
Hi Karl,

I have been using RQTL2 for my QTL analysis. I like how the LOCO approach get rid of a lot of "noise".

I have a couple of questions though:

1) I'm preparing my LOD plots for the chromosomes of interest, however I haven't been able to include "ticks" in marker positions as the ones in RQTL. Do you have any trick that can help me with that issue?

2) I have 7 years of data for 2 traits (24 traits in the model). As summary plot, I would like to average the 7 LOD scores for each trait and use the average in a "summary" LOD plot. I have been able to export the scan1 result (with LOCO) to an excel file with the LOD score at each position (pseudo markers + markers). But I haven't been able to, after adding the averages, make a plot using the map with pseudo markers created by the program.

For now I exported the map and scan1 results, so I can work on them and map using another program. However I would like to have the figure with the same nice format of the ones created by plot_scan1...

3) Is there any article to reference RQTL2? I know is fairly new, but I wander if you have any preferred way to cite it...

Thanks in advance!

Nico

parts: > 1) I'm preparing my LOD plots for the chromosomes of interest, however I haven't been able to include "ticks" in marker positions as the ones in RQTL. Do you have any trick that can help me with that issue?

The data vis part of R/qtl2 is not yet well developed. And I had in mind mostly high-dimensional data, where the marker ticks end up being a big black bar.

In the short term, probably the easiest thing is to use qtl2convert::scan_qtl2_to_qtl() to convert the genome scan calculated by R/qtl2 into the format used by R/qtl1, and then use the R/qtl1 functions to make your plot.

> 2) I have 7 years of data for 2 traits (24 traits in the model). As summary plot, I would like to average the 7 LOD scores for each trait and use the average in a "summary" LOD plot. I have been able to export the scan1 result (with LOCO) to an excel file with the LOD score at each position (pseudo markers + markers). But I haven't been able to, after adding the averages, make a plot using the map with pseudo markers created by the program.
>
> For now I exported the map and scan1 results, so I can work on them and map using another program. However I would like to have the figure with the same nice format of the ones created by plot_scan1...

It requires a bit of messing about, but I'd try calculating the averages within R. The main trick is preserving the "scan1" class and other attributes.

library(qtl2geno)
library(qtl2scan)
iron <- read_cross2(system.file("extdata", "iron.zip", package="qtl2geno"))
Xcovar <- get_x_covar(iron)
map <- insert_pseudomarkers(iron$gmap, step=1)
pr <- calc_genoprob(iron, map)
out <- scan1(pr, iron$pheno, Xcovar=Xcovar)

# make a copy of the scan1 output
out_avelod <- out
# replace the first column with the row means
out_avelod[,1] <- rowMeans(out)
# change the name
colnames(out_avelod)[1] <- "aveLOD"

# cbind the original results with the first column of the copy
out <- cbind(out, subset(out_avelod, lod=1))
> 3) Is there any article to reference RQTL2? I know is fairly new, but I wander if you have any preferred way to cite it...

Not yet. I guess just cite the website, http://kbroman.org/qtl2

kind regards,
karl
